questions.question_text: Two tangents drawn from a point PPP touch a circle with center OOO at points QQQ and RRR. Points AAA and BBB lie on PQPQPQ and PRPRPR, respectively, such that ABABAB is also a tangent to the same circle. If ∠AOB=50∘\angle AOB = 50^\circ∠AOB=50∘, then ∠APB\angle APB∠APB, in degrees, equals
questions.explanation_text:
Two tangents PQPQPQ and PRPRPR are drawn from an external point PPP to a circle with center OOO, touching the circle at QQQ and RRR. Points AAA and BBB lie on PQPQPQ and PRPRPR respectively, and ABABAB is also tangent to the circle. Let ABABAB touch the circle at point TTT.

Since two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length, the line joining that external point to the center bisects the angle between the two tangents.

From point AAA, the two tangents to the circle are AQAQAQ and ATATAT.

So OAOAOA bisects ∠QAT\angle QAT∠QAT, meaning ∠OAQ=∠OAT=α\angle OAQ = \angle OAT = \alpha∠OAQ=∠OAT=α.

From point BBB, the two tangents to the circle are BRBRBR and BTBTBT.

So OBOBOB bisects ∠RBT\angle RBT∠RBT, meaning ∠OBR=∠OBT=β\angle OBR = \angle OBT = \beta∠OBR=∠OBT=β.

Since TTT lies on segment ABABAB, we get ∠QAB=∠QAT=2α\angle QAB = \angle QAT = 2\alpha∠QAB=∠QAT=2α.

Since AAA lies on line PQPQPQ:

∠PAB=180∘−2α\angle PAB = 180^\circ - 2\alpha∠PAB=180∘−2α

Similarly:

∠PBA=180∘−2β\angle PBA = 180^\circ - 2\beta∠PBA=180∘−2β

In △OAB\triangle OAB△OAB:

∠OAB+∠OBA+∠AOB=180∘\angle OAB + \angle OBA + \angle AOB = 180^\circ∠OAB+∠OBA+∠AOB=180∘

α+β=180∘−50∘=130∘\alpha + \beta = 180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circα+β=180∘−50∘=130∘

In △PAB\triangle PAB△PAB:

∠APB+∠PAB+∠PBA=180∘\angle APB + \angle PAB + \angle PBA = 180^\circ∠APB+∠PAB+∠PBA=180∘

∠APB+(180∘−2α)+(180∘−2β)=180∘\angle APB + (180^\circ - 2\alpha) + (180^\circ - 2\beta) = 180^\circ∠APB+(180∘−2α)+(180∘−2β)=180∘

∠APB=2(α+β)−180∘\angle APB = 2(\alpha + \beta) - 180^\circ∠APB=2(α+β)−180∘

∠APB=2(130∘)−180∘\angle APB = 2(130^\circ) - 180^\circ∠APB=2(130∘)−180∘

∠APB=80∘\angle APB = 80^\circ∠APB=80∘

questions.question_text: Suppose a,b,ca,b,ca,b,c are three distinct natural numbers, such that 3ac=8(a+b)3ac = 8(a+b)3ac=8(a+b). Then, the smallest possible value of 3a+2b+c3a+2b+c3a+2b+c is
questions.explanation_text:
From 3ac=8(a+b)3ac = 8(a+b)3ac=8(a+b), we can express bbb in terms of aaa and ccc:

3ac=8a+8b3ac = 8a + 8b3ac=8a+8b

8b=3ac−8a8b = 3ac - 8a8b=3ac−8a

b=a(3c−8)8b = \dfrac{a(3c - 8)}{8}b=8a(3c−8)​

Since bbb must be a natural number, 888 must divide a(3c−8)a(3c - 8)a(3c−8), and 3c−8>03c - 8 > 03c−8>0 which means c≥3c \geq 3c≥3.

Also, aaa, bbb, ccc must all be distinct.

Substituting bbb into 3a+2b+c3a + 2b + c3a+2b+c:

3a+2b+c=3a+2a(3c−8)8+c=a(4+3c)4+c3a + 2b + c = 3a + \dfrac{2a(3c - 8)}{8} + c = \dfrac{a(4 + 3c)}{4} + c3a+2b+c=3a+82a(3c−8)​+c=4a(4+3c)​+c

To minimise this, we want small values of aaa and ccc. We try small values of ccc systematically.

c=3c = 3c=3:

b=a(1)8=a8b = \dfrac{a(1)}{8} = \dfrac{a}{8}b=8a(1)​=8a​

Smallest valid a=8a = 8a=8, giving b=1b = 1b=1. All distinct.

3(8)+2(1)+3=293(8) + 2(1) + 3 = 293(8)+2(1)+3=29

c=4c = 4c=4:

b=a(4)8=a2b = \dfrac{a(4)}{8} = \dfrac{a}{2}b=8a(4)​=2a​

Smallest valid a=2a = 2a=2, giving b=1b = 1b=1. All distinct.

Verification: 3(2)(4)=243(2)(4) = 243(2)(4)=24 and 8(2+1)=248(2 + 1) = 248(2+1)=24 ✓

3(2)+2(1)+4=123(2) + 2(1) + 4 = 123(2)+2(1)+4=12

c=5c = 5c=5:

b=7a8b = \dfrac{7a}{8}b=87a​

Smallest valid a=8a = 8a=8, giving b=7b = 7b=7. All distinct.

3(8)+2(7)+5=433(8) + 2(7) + 5 = 433(8)+2(7)+5=43

c=6c = 6c=6:

b=10a8=5a4b = \dfrac{10a}{8} = \dfrac{5a}{4}b=810a​=45a​

Smallest valid a=4a = 4a=4, giving b=5b = 5b=5. All distinct.

3(4)+2(5)+6=283(4) + 2(5) + 6 = 283(4)+2(5)+6=28

As ccc grows beyond 444, the values keep increasing. The case c=4c = 4c=4, a=2a = 2a=2, b=1b = 1b=1 gives the smallest result.

The smallest possible value of 3a+2b+c=123a + 2b + c = \boxed{12}3a+2b+c=12​

questions.question_text: The average number of copies of a book sold per day by a shopkeeper is 60 in the initial seven days and 63 in the initial eight days, after the book launch. On the ninth day, she sells 11 copies less than the eighth day, and the average number of copies sold per day from second day to ninth day becomes 66. The number of copies sold on the first day of the book launch is
questions.explanation_text:
Average of first 7 days = 60, so total copies in 7 days:

=60×7=420= 60 \times 7 = 420=60×7=420

Average of first 8 days = 63, so total copies in 8 days:

=63×8=504= 63 \times 8 = 504=63×8=504

Copies sold on Day 8:

d8=504−420=84d_8 = 504 - 420 = 84d8​=504−420=84

Copies sold on Day 9:

d9=84−11=73d_9 = 84 - 11 = 73d9​=84−11=73

Average from Day 2 to Day 9 = 66, so total copies from Day 2 to Day 9:

=66×8=528= 66 \times 8 = 528=66×8=528

Total copies from Day 2 to Day 8:

=528−73=455= 528 - 73 = 455=528−73=455

From the first 8 days total:

d1+(d2+d3+d4+d5+d6+d7+d8)=504d_1 + (d_2 + d_3 + d_4 + d_5 + d_6 + d_7 + d_8) = 504d1​+(d2​+d3​+d4​+d5​+d6​+d7​+d8​)=504

d1+455=504d_1 + 455 = 504d1​+455=504

d1=504−455d_1 = 504 - 455d1​=504−455

d1=49d_1 = 49d1​=49

questions.question_text: If mmm and nnn are integers such that (m+2n)(2m+n)=27(m+2n)(2m+n) = 27(m+2n)(2m+n)=27, then the maximum possible value of 2m−3n2m-3n2m−3n is
questions.explanation_text:
Given that mmm and nnn are integers and (m+2n)(2m+n)=27(m+2n)(2m+n) = 27(m+2n)(2m+n)=27.

Since both factors are integers, we list all integer factor pairs (a,b)(a, b)(a,b) such that a×b=27a \times b = 27a×b=27:

(1,27), (27,1), (3,9), (9,3), (−1,−27), (−27,−1), (−3,−9), (−9,−3)(1, 27),\ (27, 1),\ (3, 9),\ (9, 3),\ (-1, -27),\ (-27, -1),\ (-3, -9),\ (-9, -3)(1,27), (27,1), (3,9), (9,3), (−1,−27), (−27,−1), (−3,−9), (−9,−3)

Let m+2n=am + 2n = am+2n=a and 2m+n=b2m + n = b2m+n=b.

From these two equations:

3m=2b−a  ⟹  m=2b−a33m = 2b - a \implies m = \dfrac{2b - a}{3}3m=2b−a⟹m=32b−a​

3n=2a−b  ⟹  n=2a−b33n = 2a - b \implies n = \dfrac{2a - b}{3}3n=2a−b⟹n=32a−b​

For mmm and nnn to be integers, both (2b−a)(2b - a)(2b−a) and (2a−b)(2a - b)(2a−b) must be divisible by 3. This happens only when (a+b)(a + b)(a+b) is divisible by 3.

Checking each factor pair for this condition:

(1,27)→a+b=28(1, 27) \rightarrow a + b = 28(1,27)→a+b=28 -- not divisible by 3

(27,1)→a+b=28(27, 1) \rightarrow a + b = 28(27,1)→a+b=28 -- not divisible by 3

(3,9)→a+b=12(3, 9) \rightarrow a + b = 12(3,9)→a+b=12 -- divisible by 3

(9,3)→a+b=12(9, 3) \rightarrow a + b = 12(9,3)→a+b=12 -- divisible by 3

(−1,−27)→a+b=−28(-1, -27) \rightarrow a + b = -28(−1,−27)→a+b=−28 -- not divisible by 3

(−27,−1)→a+b=−28(-27, -1) \rightarrow a + b = -28(−27,−1)→a+b=−28 -- not divisible by 3

(−3,−9)→a+b=−12(-3, -9) \rightarrow a + b = -12(−3,−9)→a+b=−12 -- divisible by 3

(−9,−3)→a+b=−12(-9, -3) \rightarrow a + b = -12(−9,−3)→a+b=−12 -- divisible by 3

Only 4 pairs give integer solutions.

For (a,b)=(3,9)(a, b) = (3, 9)(a,b)=(3,9):

m=18−33=5m = \dfrac{18 - 3}{3} = 5m=318−3​=5, n=6−93=−1\quad n = \dfrac{6 - 9}{3} = -1n=36−9​=−1

2m−3n=10+3=132m - 3n = 10 + 3 = 132m−3n=10+3=13

For (a,b)=(9,3)(a, b) = (9, 3)(a,b)=(9,3):

m=6−93=−1m = \dfrac{6 - 9}{3} = -1m=36−9​=−1, n=18−33=5\quad n = \dfrac{18 - 3}{3} = 5n=318−3​=5

2m−3n=−2−15=−172m - 3n = -2 - 15 = -172m−3n=−2−15=−17

For (a,b)=(−3,−9)(a, b) = (-3, -9)(a,b)=(−3,−9):

m=−18+33=−5m = \dfrac{-18 + 3}{3} = -5m=3−18+3​=−5, n=−6+93=1\quad n = \dfrac{-6 + 9}{3} = 1n=3−6+9​=1

2m−3n=−10−3=−132m - 3n = -10 - 3 = -132m−3n=−10−3=−13

For (a,b)=(−9,−3)(a, b) = (-9, -3)(a,b)=(−9,−3):

m=−6+93=1m = \dfrac{-6 + 9}{3} = 1m=3−6+9​=1, n=−18+33=−5\quad n = \dfrac{-18 + 3}{3} = -5n=3−18+3​=−5

2m−3n=2+15=172m - 3n = 2 + 15 = 172m−3n=2+15=17

The possible values of 2m−3n2m - 3n2m−3n are: −17, −13, 13, 17-17,\ -13,\ 13,\ 17−17, −13, 13, 17

The maximum possible value of 2m−3n=172m - 3n = 172m−3n=17

questions.question_text: Rita and Sneha can row a boat at 5 km/h and 6 km/h in still water, respectively. Sneha's downstream speed =(6+v)= (6 + v)=(6+v) km/h

146−v−146+v=4860=45\dfrac{14}{6 - v} - \dfrac{14}{6 + v} = \dfrac{48}{60} = \dfrac{4}{5}6−v14​−6+v14​=6048​=54​ hours

14((6+v)−(6−v)(6−v)(6+v))=4514\left(\dfrac{(6+v) - (6-v)}{(6-v)(6+v)}\right) = \dfrac{4}{5}14((6−v)(6+v)(6+v)−(6−v)​)=54​

28v36−v2=45\dfrac{28v}{36 - v^2} = \dfrac{4}{5}36−v228v​=54​

140v=144−4v2140v = 144 - 4v^2140v=144−4v2

4v2+140v−144=04v^2 + 140v - 144 = 04v2+140v−144=0

v2+35v−36=0v^2 + 35v - 36 = 0v2+35v−36=0

(v+36)(v−1)=0(v + 36)(v - 1) = 0(v+36)(v−1)=0

v=1v = 1v=1 km/h (since speed cannot be negative)

Rita goes upstream a distance ddd km, then returns downstream the same distance ddd km.

Rita's upstream speed =5−1=4= 5 - 1 = 4=5−1=4 km/h

Rita's downstream speed =5+1=6= 5 + 1 = 6=5+1=6 km/h

Total time =100= 100=100 minutes =53= \dfrac{5}{3}=35​ hours

d4+d6=53\dfrac{d}{4} + \dfrac{d}{6} = \dfrac{5}{3}4d​+6d​=35​

3d+2d12=53\dfrac{3d + 2d}{12} = \dfrac{5}{3}123d+2d​=35​

5d12=53\dfrac{5d}{12} = \dfrac{5}{3}125d​=35​

d=53×125d = \dfrac{5}{3} \times \dfrac{12}{5}d=35​×512​

d=4d = 4d=4 km

Total distance =d+d=4+4=8= d + d = 4 + 4 = 8=d+d=4+4=8 km

where b1b_1b1​ and b2b_2b2​ are the parallel sides and hhh is the perpendicular distance between them.

PQ=∣34−(−34)∣=32PQ = \left|\dfrac{3}{4} - \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right)\right| = \dfrac{3}{2}PQ=​43​−(−43​)​=23​

h=32−34=34h = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}h=23​​−43​​=43​​

So,

AreaPBCQ=12×(1+32)×34=12×52×34=5316\text{Area}_{PBCQ} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}\right) \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{16}AreaPBCQ​=21​×(1+23​)×43​​=21​×25​×43​​=1653​​
